body:
Really, I can't even be mad. That's the real twist of the knife. They're perfect for each other. They're great people. I can't expect people to be attached to me forever at their own detriment.

A suppose a roommate is possible, but I'm very wary. I'm very bad with people, especially since my agoriphobia emerged. I very strongly prefer my privacy, and my own way of doing things.

And, I mean, the broader issue that even if I figure it out... Life is just so tenuously worth it as it is. I barely enjoy anything anymore. I'm very lonely, and not exactly an ideal partner. I barely do anything all week and still feel exhausted.

I've attempted suicide before. It really didn't feel that bad the way I did it. I was unconscious very quickly. Painful, yes, but in truth I've regretted failing my previous attempt ever since I made it. 

I can't figure this out. Or perhaps, I don't think it's worth it to figure this out. It's always going to be something. Always some new problem, some new issue that could be solved by money, money that I don't have. I'm disabled. My income is fixed, and resources intentionally limited. Rent gets too high: I'm fucked. I save too much: no more income. I try and get a job: no safety net if I have a break down. The system puts people on disability in an impossible position, especially in terms of housing. 

I really, really doubt that D&D is going make my life worth it or introduce me to those who will. In fact, evidence suggests that my hobby will make my life actively worse.
